title: What the State set aside for federal deferrals, and what came
question: Did the State’s Medi-Cal estimates budget for the federal deferrals that then arrived?
finding: In November 2025 the State budgeted $100.0 million of General Fund in 2026-27 to repay deferrals of benefit claims ($25 million a quarter) and $0 for administrative deferrals, saying the administrative deferrals would no longer continue. The federal letters then withheld $162.9 million, $158.2 million, $143.8 million of administrative claims in the three quarters ended 2025-12-31, 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30, and $15.9 million, $24.8 million, $2.6 million on immigration-status benefit items, close to the $25 million a quarter assumed. In May 2026 the State raised the 2026-27 figures to $200.0 million and $145.0 million, and its 2025-26 figures to $477.7 million and $582.4 million. Neither estimate has a line for the $2.87 billion withheld on personal care.
how: State figures: General Fund amounts in the “current year compared to budget year” tables of the November 2025 and May 2026 Medi-Cal estimates, by policy-change number (2034 benefit deferrals, 2123 administrative deferrals, 2415 and 2559 State-only claiming). Federal figures: sums of the deferral letters’ lines (federal share), grouped as in the first screen. The comparison is this project’s; the November estimate’s repayment schedule by federal quarter is in the rows.
limits: The State repays a deferral in General Fund dollars and gets the money back if the deferral is released, so a budget line is a cash estimate, not an admission. Federal quarters (October to September) do not line up with State fiscal years (July to June). Whether the State counts the personal-care deferral under another line, or treats it as cash it expects back, is not said in these files. The State may also have budgeted in documents not on disk.
